items.title: HIV-1 diagnosis during pre-exposure prophylaxis: A case report.
items.authors: Cruces L, Baquero L, Barletta JAE, Turk G, Laufer N.
items.abstract: We report a case of HIV diagnosis in a 36-year-old man who has sex with men receiving daily oral PrEP (emtricitabine/tenofovir) in Argentina, where viral load or HIV PCR testing is not routinely available before or during prophylaxis. In 2022, PrEP was initiated after a diagnosis of primary syphilis, with a non-reactive fourth-generation HIV test performed 13 days earlier (outside the recommended window), so very early infection already present at initiation cannot be excluded. Self-reported adherence was >95%. Serology was negative at day 23 and became reactive at day 73, with an indeterminate Western blot (gp120 only), undetectable plasma HIV-RNA and preserved lymphocyte counts; dolutegravir was added to complete antiretroviral treatment. Standard diagnostic algorithms were initially inconclusive, and confirmation required approaches beyond routine practice: HIV-1 RNA was detected only after ultracentrifugation of 14 mL of plasma (55 copies), and low-level proviral HIV-1 DNA was identified after analysis of an extensive number of cells; Nef- and p24-specific T-cell responses were also detected. No resistance-associated mutations were found on proviral DNA (integrase region). The Western blot eventually became positive at day 382, while a rapid immunochromatographic assay remained negative at 34 months. Atypical presentations of this kind have been reported under oral TDF/FTC PrEP and were subsequently characterized as long-acting early viral inhibition (LEVI) syndrome, predominantly in the context of long-acting cabotegravir. The present case illustrates the extent of non-routine investigation required to confirm HIV acquisition, and the challenges this poses in settings where oral PrEP is the only available option and HIV-1 RNA PCR cannot be routinely deployed. PrEP should be initiated promptly following a negative HIV test performed on the same day, or as close as possible to PrEP initiation, particularly when recent exposure is possible. HIV testing should be repeated sequentially after initiation, and discordant results should prompt continued serological and molecular evaluation.

items.title: Immune Imprinting Across Respiratory Virus Infection, Vaccination, and Passive Immunization: Rethinking 'Original Antigenic Sin' in Influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV.
items.authors: Szuster-Ciesielska A.
items.abstract: Immune imprinting shapes every subsequent response to antigenically related pathogens and is now central to designing updated vaccines for influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The label "Original Antigenic Sin" has framed imprinting as a fixed liability, but recent germinal-center, B-cell repertoire, and epidemiological data show that the effect is neither uniformly harmful nor irreversible. This review distinguishes cross-reactive immune memory from immune imprinting, defined here as a preferential bias toward the first-encountered antigen. Prior exposure can provide useful cross-reactive memory, but available evidence generally does not show that first-antigen bias itself improves protection relative to an equivalent unbiased memory response. We therefore use a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework to examine how antigenic distance, conserved-epitope accessibility, and exposure interval may influence both the usefulness of recalled memory and the extent to which imprinting restricts recruitment of responses to later antigens. The framework organizes existing observations and is not intended to predict imprinting outcomes ex ante. We discuss recent quantitative models that explicitly formalize competition between memory and de novo responses as complementary, pathogen-specific approaches. Across influenza and SARS-CoV-2, early exposure can establish cross-reactive memory associated with subsequent heterologous protection, while preferential recall of the priming antigen may limit responses to novel epitopes. For RSV, the effects of maternal vaccination and passive antibodies on subsequent active immune memory remain uncertain. Immunogen engineering, schedule adjustment, adjuvant selection, and cohort-tailored strategies may broaden pre-existing memory toward conserved protective epitopes and reduce restrictive first-antigen bias.

items.title: Microneedle-mediated co-delivery of biomimetic melanin and pro-regenerative factors for oxidative and immune modulation in vitiligo.
items.authors: Liang J, Liu W, Jiang Y, Yu Y, Li Q, Zhang Y, Li W, Zhang X.
items.abstract: Vitiligo lesions are characterized by elevated epidermal oxidative stress, cytotoxic immune activation, and impaired melanogenesis, while conventional topical therapies often fail to modulate these pathogenic events due to limited skin penetration and therapeutic depth. To address these challenges, a dual-layer gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/hyaluronic acid methacryloyl (HAMA)//hyaluronic acid (HA) (Gel//HA) microneedle system was engineered. The inner HA layer rapidly dissolves upon insertion, releasing keratinocyte-membrane-coated artificial melanin nanoparticles (MPDA) to achieve early reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and targeted delivery to keratinocytes. The outer Gel hydrogel layer enables sustained intradermal delivery of basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) and tyrosinase (TYR), supporting melanocyte survival and restoring melanin synthesis. The microneedles exhibited robust mechanical strength (0.234 ± 0.014 N/needle) with a penetration depth of approximately 300-350 μm. In vitro, the cumulative release of bFGF and TYR reached 65% and 70% within the first 72 h, respectively, and subsequently increased more gradually to 92.1% and 90.7% by day 21. In vitro, the combined administration of MPDA, bFGF, and TYR, mitigated H2O2-induced oxidative injury and enhanced keratinocyte viability. In a monobenzone-induced mouse model, Gel@bFGF/TYR//HA@MPDA treatment markedly promoted repigmentation, restored epidermal melanin deposition, and reduced the expression of CD8, IFN-γ, and TNF-α. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed suppression of ferroptosis-related genes and reactivation of the Wnt-Frizzled-MITF melanogenic signaling axis. This spatially designed microneedle system provides coordinated antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and pro-melanogenic effects, offering a promising localized therapeutic strategy for vitiligo.

Veterinary drug residues in animal-derived foods: From analytical detection to intelligent and sustainable surveillance.
items.authors: Ramezani Farani M, Mirzaee D, Voosough A, Hatami A, Chanmey K, Miraei Ashtiani SH, Sheik A, Alipourfard I, Ch Stratakos A, A Piletsky S, Hwang SK, Huh YS.
items.abstract: Veterinary drug residues in animal-derived foods remain a major challenge for food safety, public health, and international trade. This review examines residue control through the complementary roles of analytical technologies, digital tools and green analytical chemistry. Rapid screening can support local decisions, while liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry provides laboratory confirmation. Digital tools offer opportunities to connect analytical results with treatment records and product traceability, but their value depends on data quality, interoperability and validation. Solvent reduction and miniaturization should be assessed alongside energy use and material life cycles. The proposed farm-to-fork roadmap links these approaches with regulatory requirements and One Health priorities, emphasizing reliable measurements, coordinated data use and feasibility in resource-constrained settings.

items.title: Trends in and program characteristics associated with pre-exposure prophylaxis availability among opioid treatment facilities in the United States.
items.authors: Figgatt MC, Jaiswal J, Alnashri Y, Rosen JG, Rich JD, Green TC.
items.abstract:
Objective

To examine the prevalence and settings of PrEP availability at opioid use treatment facilities in the United States.

Methods

We examined PrEP trends from 2021 to 2024 using the National Substance Use and Mental Health Services Survey. Using multivariable logistic regression models, we calculated odds ratios (OR) and their 95% confidence intervals (CI) to examine associations between facility characteristics and PrEP prescribing in 2024.

Results

A total of 13,755 substance use treatment facilities in 2021; 14,201 in 2022; 12,892 in 2023; and 13,875 in 2024 were included. The percentage of facilities offering PrEP increased from 6.03% in 2021 to 10.62% in 2024 (p < 0.01) nationwide. Despite comprising over 90% of facilities, outpatient (8.57%) and residential (14.26%) facilities had lower PrEP availability than inpatient facilities (23.19%). Facilities with methadone and buprenorphine had higher odds of PrEP availability (methadone OR = 7.52, 95% CI = 5.34, 10.59; buprenorphine only OR = 10.09, 95% CI = 7.53, 13.52) compared to those without these treatments. Facilities offering programs specific to people living with HIV (OR = 2.32, 95% CI = 1.83, 2.94) and those identifying as LGBTQ+ (OR = 1.75, 95% CI = 1.35, 2.27) were more likely to offer PrEP.

Conclusions

Despite the high number of people served in outpatient and residential facilities, PrEP access continues to remain low.

items.title: Nanomaterials Reshaping Tumor Metabolism: A New Frontier to Overcome T Cell Exhaustion.
items.authors: Zhu X, He L, Li J, Guo S, Liu X, Cao Y, Song S.
items.abstract: Adoptive antitumor immunity ultimately fails because metabolically hostile tumor microenvironments (TME) drive T cells into a dysfunctional exhausted state that current checkpoint blockade only partially reverses. Crucially, the principal metabolic stresses - accumulation of lactate, lipids and adenosine, deprivation of glucose and amino acids, and hypoxia - do not act in isolation but form a densely cross-regulated network that progressively reinforces T cell exhaustion. This review synthesizes how each barrier arises and how they amplify one another, then maps nanomaterial-based countermeasures onto this network: catalytic nanomaterials that degrade lactate and adenosine, lipid-modulating and mitochondria-targeted formulations, amino-acid replenishment systems, and hypoxia-relieving designs that pair metabolic correction with checkpoint inhibition or photodynamic therapy. Particular attention is given to the design principles - tissue targeting, stimuli-responsive release and rational combination - that determine whether metabolic reprogramming yields durable restoration of T cell function rather than transient phenotypic rescue. Emerging preclinical evidence indicates that nanomaterial-mediated metabolic remodeling can convert the immunosuppressive TME into an immune-supportive niche and recover effector function of exhausted T cells. We further identify the key gaps that currently limit clinical translation: the absence of subset-level evaluation distinguishing reversible progenitor-like exhausted T cells from terminally exhausted cells, the lack of epigenetic endpoints such as histone lactylation, off-target metabolic suppression of T cells themselves, and the manufacturing and safety hurdles of clinical-grade nanomaterials. Resolving these issues would establish metabolic reprogramming as a credible frontier for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Numerous linked cases of acute genotype F hepatitis B virus infections in people living with HIV or on pre-exposure prophylaxis.
items.authors: Rouget R, Leducq V, Maylin S, Gozlan J, Thibault V, Valantin MA, Mercier-Delarue S, Faycal A, Valin N, Wirden M, Cocherie T, Akhavan S, Roque-Afonso AM, Sayon S, Chevaliez S, Bouille T, Fauchois A, Calvez V, Marcelin AG, Lacombe K, Delaugerre C, Pourcher V, Manda V, Seang S, Todesco E.
items.abstract:
Objectives

At least 2.7 million people living with HIV are infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) worldwide. Some antiretroviral treatments and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-based pre-exposure prophylaxis protect against HBV infection. However, emerging antiretroviral strategies without any activity against HBV may promote spread of this virus in the future. In this context, we studied recent cases of acute HBV infection in people at risk of sexually transmitted infections. Our objective was to better understand HBV circulation and the dynamics of its transmission.

Methods

This retrospective study included people diagnosed with acute HBV infections between 2022 and 2025 in France. The whole HBV genome was amplified and sequenced by next-generation sequencing for network analysis.

Results

Sixteen men, with a median age of 35 years, were enrolled. Six were living with HIV, including three receiving long-acting injectable cabotegravir/rilpivirine treatment. Four of the HIV-negative individuals were taking pre-exposure prophylaxis. Nine had been vaccinated against HBV, and six had anti-HBs antibody titres between 10 and 100 IU/L. Analysis revealed HBV genotype F1b in 14 patients, with very high homology among the viruses. No known immune escape mutations were identified, even in the individuals with anti-HBs antibodies.

Conclusions

A transmission cluster of HBV F1b genotype was observed in a population at risk of infection. This genotype, which is endemic to Latin America, is rarely detected in France. These findings may serve as a timely reminder of the ongoing circulation of HBV among exposed populations. HBV transmission among vaccinated individuals with positive anti-HBs antibodies raises questions and should be further studied.

items.title: Development and implementation of a pharmacy PrEP awareness-raising and referral pathway: acceptability and feasibility of a UK pilot.
items.authors: Harrison C, Harryman L, Stockwell S, Family H, Kesten JM, Denford S, Scott J, Sabin C, Copping J, Saunders J, Hamilton-Shaw R, Symonds N, Dick OB, Tarmey E, Horwood J.

items.title: A scoping review of pre-exposure prophylaxis awareness, acceptability, uptake, adherence, and HIV-related risk behaviors among university students in South Africa.
items.authors: Serebane MJ, Ramavhoya TI, Mutshatshi TE, Mokhwelepa LW.
items.abstract:
Background

Pre-exposure prophylaxis is an effective biomedical intervention for preventing HIV infection, yet evidence on its awareness, acceptability, uptake and adherence among South African university students remains fragmented.

Objective

To map and synthesize the available evidence on pre-exposure prophylaxis awareness, acceptability, uptake, adherence, and HIV-related risk behaviors among university students in South Africa.

Methods

A scoping review was conducted using Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Studies published between 2014 and 2026 were searched in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, CINAHL, African Journals Online and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses/grey literature. Two reviewers independently screened studies and charted data using a predefined extraction tool. Findings were synthesized thematically.

Results

Sixteen studies were included, of which 68.75% (n = 11) were quantitative and 31.25% (n = 5) qualitative. Evidence was concentrated in KwaZulu-Natal, Gauteng, Limpopo and the Western Cape, with most studies published from 2019 onwards. Six themes emerged: (1) Individual Level: individual perceptions, knowledge and appraisal of HIV and PrEP; (2) Interpersonal Level: interpersonal relationships and social influence on PrEP decision-making; (3) Institutional Level: accessibility, acceptability and responsiveness of PrEP services; (4) Community/social Level: stigma, misconceptions and social norms surrounding PrEP; (5) Structural Level: socioeconomic and health-system conditions shaping PrEP utilization; and (6) HIV Risk Behaviors: patterns of sexual risk and their relationship to PrEP need. Awareness and willingness to use PrEP were generally favorable, but uptake and sustained use were constrained by knowledge gaps, low perceived risk, stigma, side-effect concerns, cost, accessibility and service-related barriers. Risk behaviors included multiple partnerships, inconsistent condom use, substance-associated sexual behavior and socioeconomic pressures.

Conclusion

PrEP utilization is shaped by interacting individual, social, institutional and structural factors. Integrated, youth-friendly services and targeted education addressing HIV risk, stigma and access are needed to strengthen informed PrEP decision-making and prevention.

items.title: HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis in US prison settings: a model-based cost-effectiveness study.
items.authors: Park Y, Goldhaber-Fiebert JD, Cipriano LE.
items.abstract:
Background

HIV prevalence in prisons is three times higher than in the general community, and ongoing transmission risks highlight the importance of prevention, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). We evaluated the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of prison-based PrEP programs in four US states.

Methods

We developed a dynamic compartmental model simulating HIV transmission in both general and incarcerated populations, instantiated for four representative US states (standardized population of five million people). We assessed five strategies involving PrEP for specific risk groups in prison compared to the status quo of no PrEP. We assumed 25% uptake among eligible individuals for 20 years. We estimated total lifetime costs (in 2024 USD) and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), discounted at 3% annually, incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), and HIV infections averted from a healthcare sector perspective.

Findings

In Washington, New York, and Georgia, providing PrEP to 25% of people who inject drugs (PWID) in prison prevented 12%-14% of new infections in incarcerated people, and 0.01%-0.02% of new infections in the community, and was cost-saving compared to no PrEP. Expanding eligibility to all high-risk persons (PWID and men who have sex with men (MSM)) prevented more infections and cost less than $60,000 per QALY gained compared to more restrictive policies. In California, where the epidemic is concentrated among MSM rather than PWID, providing PrEP to only MSM costs $32,000 per QALY gained.

Interpretation

Prison-based PrEP programs can be cost-saving or cost-effective, averting infections within and outside the prison system. These findings support expanding access to PrEP in prisons, with implementation and funding decisions guided by local HIV epidemiology.

Funding

Canada Research Chairs Program, Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada, National Institute on Drug Abuse.

items.title: Methodological considerations for indirect treatment comparisons of HIV incidence for long-acting injectable pre-exposure prophylaxis.
items.authors: Curteis T, Franklin AN, Judge RK, Zolotor A, Jarrett J, Carter CC, Ebrahimi R, Mezzio D.
items.abstract: Background: Given the effectiveness of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), the HIV prevention landscape is expanding rapidly - including recently approved injectable options which have shown high efficacy in clinical trials. As head-to-head trials of injectable PrEPs are not feasible, indirect treatment comparisons (ITCs) are of value to generate comparative estimates of efficacy and safety. However, several methodological challenges must be carefully considered when conducting these ITCs. This review outlines these complexities to support informed decision-making. Main text: We identified methodological considerations through a narrative review of available literature (including leveraging published systematic reviews), evidence from PrEP trials and, where applicable, reference to methodological guidelines. Our review suggests treatment effect modifiers (TEMs) for PrEP are poorly defined in the HIV PrEP literature and, due to the high efficacy of injectable compared with oral PrEP, encompass potential prognostic factors (such as background HIV incidence). Challenges in comparing potential TEMs across trials were also noted due to, for example, differences in measurement methodology and reporting timepoint for adherence. Accounting for variation in follow-up across studies within potential ITCs is critical as HIV acquisition is a rare, time-dependent event. Additionally, zero or few events occur within injectable PrEP trials in HIV, challenging variance estimation and necessitating alternative statistical approaches. Population-adjustment methods are similarly complicated. Conclusions: This review outlines key considerations and offers practical recommendations to inform robust conduct of ITCs of PrEP, and support the interpretation of results. Areas of further research to strengthen future comparative evidence are also highlighted.

items.title: Readiness to start long acting injectable HIV treatment and prevention and conditions for acceptance among clinic clients in Uganda
items.authors: Olet SC, Muluga WU, Musoki D, Kihumuro BR, Muluga F, Ssebandeke I, Among F, Stecher CD, Musoke D.
items.abstract: Long-acting injectable human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) medicines expand treatment and prevention choices, but willingness to use them does not establish readiness to begin. We examined readiness to start these options, associated factors and conditions for acceptance among people living with HIV and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)-service clients in Uganda. This cross-sectional study analysed 225 participants at Mildmay Hospital and Kajjansi Health Centre IV in central Uganda. Readiness meant preferring initiation immediately or within three months. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), including age-by-service-group interaction. Separate models examined informational, perceptual and financial factors, adjusting for service group, age and sex. Logistic marginal standardisation checked demographic and expanded age comparisons. Overall, 108 participants (48.0%) were ready to start injectable HIV treatment or prevention, 111 (49.3%) wanted more information about these options, and six (2.7%) preferred initiation in six to twelve months. Readiness was 80.8% among people living with HIV aged 15–24 years and 34.4% among those aged 25 years or older (aPR 2.35, 95% CI 1.63–3.38). Corresponding proportions among PrEP-service clients were 39.2% and 41.4% (aPR 0.95, 95% CI 0.60–1.50; interaction p=0.002). In separate adjusted models, clinic-staff information (aPR 1.94, 95% CI 1.42–2.66), belief in greater effectiveness (2.00, 1.43–2.80) and a one-point increase in benefit score (3.27, 2.36–4.55) were associated with higher readiness. A one-point increase in concern score (0.70, 0.60–0.80) and financial difficulty sometimes or more often (0.68, 0.48–0.96) were associated with lower readiness. Fewer side effects was the leading condition for accepting injectable HIV treatment or prevention across service and readiness groups. Nearly half of participants were ready to start, while a similar proportion wanted further information about injectable options. Programmes should assess intended initiation timing alongside willingness and address safety, appointment flexibility, privacy and affordability through counselling and service planning.

items.title: Cryogenic sintering decellularized tissue particles creates porous scaffolds that support long-term alternative macrophage infiltration in large traumatic injuries.
items.authors: Baurceanu I, Pal S, Orenuga IK, Kimmel AE, Anderson CF, Magidson V, Harned A, Narayan K, Cosgriff-Hernandez E, Wolf MT.
items.abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrix (ECM) biomaterials are widely utilized in soft tissue reconstruction, triggering a Type 2 inflammatory response that promotes repair. However, it remains challenging to manipulate the geometry and porosity of native ECM forms, like sheets and particulates, without chemically altering composition. We describe a controlled freeze-drying method to cryogenically sinter ECM particles into large, mechanically stable, porous 3D ECM scaffolds without altering matrix composition. Modulating small intestinal submucosa (SIS) ECM particle concentration (50 to 200 mg/mL) and freezing rate (-30 °C to -196 °C) during sintering enabled control over 3D porosity (934-3476 μm<sup>2</sup> pore area). Moderate ECM concentrations (100 mg/mL) and slow freezing rates (-80 °C) created scaffolds with the largest pores and high mechanical stability under large strain (storage modulus 4036 ± 172 Pa). In vivo, scaffolds bridged volumetric muscle and fat pad deficits, with fabrication conditions affecting degradation and immune response between 1 and 18 weeks. Rapid CD206<sup>+</sup> macrophage infiltration occurred, particularly in 100 mg/mL -80 °C scaffolds (4752 ± 1773 macrophages/mm<sup>2</sup>). All ECM forms induced interleukin-4 (Il4) expression during the first 2 weeks (over 10-fold vs untreated), though expression in 100 mg/mL -80 °C scaffolds persisted substantially longer (8 weeks) than non-sintered particles. Small-pored 100 mg/mL -196 °C scaffolds degraded faster and remodeled into adipose tissue after 8 to 18 weeks. This study shows that ECM particulate can be processed into mechanically robust 3D scaffolds with controllable porosity and degradation without altering biochemical composition, influencing Type 2 immune activation and tissue remodeling after volumetric injury.

items.title: International Bioethics Training Program Funded by the Fogarty International Center, 2013-2023: Overview and Trends.
items.authors: Rid A, Sina B.
items.abstract: The National Institutes of Health Fogarty International Center has supported international bioethics training program funding for over two decades. This program aims to equip trainees with the knowledge and skills to serve as research ethics professionals and bioethics scholars in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and support the ethical conduct of socially valuable research in these countries. In this paper, we update a review of the program's first decade (2000-2012) and describe trends in its second decade (2013-2023), including the successful launch of PhD and post-doctoral training and increasing leadership by principal investigators from LMICs. Despite important progress, more research ethics professionals and bioethics scholars are needed to build and sustain strong bioethics infrastructure in LMICs.

items.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV: a review for dermatovenereologists.
items.authors: Pisano L, Turco M, Pimpinelli N.
items.abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection remains a significant public health issue, with 112,883 new diagnoses reported in Europe in 2023. The rise is particularly notable in Eastern Europe, where new cases increased by 20% between 2010 and 2023. Late diagnosis is a major barrier to HIV control, with nearly 50% of new infections in Europe - and up to 60% in Italy - detected at an advanced stage. Dermatovenereologists are key in early detection, as over 90% of people living with HIV show at least one HIV-related dermatologic condition before diagnosis. Thus, dermatovenereology services are well-positioned to promote routine HIV testing and prevention. Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is a highly effective HIV prevention method but is unevenly implemented across Europe. In Italy, PrEP is mostly prescribed by infectious disease specialists, except at a pioneering sexually transmitted infections (STI) center in Florence where dermatovenereologists can also prescribe it. Expanding this prescribing authority nationwide could improve access and prevention efforts among underserved populations. Integrating PrEP into dermatovenereology would enhance the continuum of care by linking STI screening, treatment, counseling, and HIV prevention, supporting UNAIDS' goal of ending AIDS by 2030. This narrative review summarizes key studies leading to PrEP approval, outlines approved administration methods for at-risk groups, discusses potential side effects, and highlights emerging therapeutic options under regulatory review (such as long-acting PrEP). It aims to equip dermatovenereologists with all the necessary tools to prescribe and manage PrEP effectively during follow-up.

items.title: Formulation-Specific Safety Issues of HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis Drugs: A Disproportionality Analysis of the FAERS Database.
items.authors: Rozza D, Poluzzi E, Antonazzo IC, Boccia A, Paccini M, Gallucci F, Ponticelli D, Geraci G, Agüero F, Mazzaglia G, Mantovani LG, Raschi E, Ferrara P.
items.abstract:
Background and objective

As human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) use expands, real-world post-marketing safety evidence remains limited, particularly regarding potential formulation-specific adverse-event patterns across oral and long-acting agents. We aimed to characterise the post-marketing safety profiles of FDA-approved PrEP drugs using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).

Methods

We conducted a disproportionality analysis using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) data from 2012 to 2024. Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) listing emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (FTC/TDF), emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (FTC/TAF) or cabotegravir (CAB) as suspected PrEP drugs were included. Two comparator groups were used: all non-PrEP ICSRs and ICSRs involving non-PrEP HIV drugs. Disproportionality was evaluated at the MedDRA high-level term (HLT) level using reporting odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), identifying signals of disproportionate reporting (SDRs) with a lower bound of the 95%CIs > 1. Sensitivity analyses explored sex, reporter type, and indication.

Results

We identified 3201 PrEP-related ICSRs (FTC/TDF: 2688; FTC/TAF: 463; CAB: 50), predominantly involving young adult males. FTC/TDF exhibited a broad pattern of SDRs-including renal/metabolic abnormalities, muscular signals, mucosal disorders and some previously under-characterised signals-many of which attenuated when using HIV-treated comparators. FTC/TAF showed a narrower, highly consistent pattern dominated by hepatobiliary and metabolic monitoring procedures, renal function evaluations and neurosensory disturbances. CAB showed specific, reproducible signals for injection-site, dermatologic and procedure-related events.

Conclusions

PrEP agents display distinct, formulation-specific and reproducible safety patterns in FAERS. Comparator choice substantially influences the detection and interpretation of SDRs and can help distinguish reproducible formulation-related reporting patterns from findings that may be driven by the clinical and reporting context. These insights highlight priority areas for future research.

items.title: HIV risk, sexual behavior and PrEP uptake, adherence and discontinuation among adolescent girls and young women in low- and middle-income countries: a scoping review.
items.authors: Ogello V, Gesesew HA, Dzando G, Ward PR.
items.abstract: Adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) bear a disproportionate burden of HIV/AIDS. Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention is limited to individuals identified as high risk following a prior risk assessment. However, AGYW with epidemiologically assessed HIV risk still struggle to align PrEP use with their sexual behaviors. This review examines how HIV risk and sexual behavior influence decisions to initiate, adhere to or discontinue PrEP. A search was conducted across five databases in November 2025. The search was registered in the Open Science Framework and followed PRISMA-SCR guidelines. A thematic content analysis approach was used to synthesize findings guided by the health belief model and COM-B framework. Forty-nine articles were eligible for synthesis. Knowledge of HIV risk and sexual behaviors motivated PrEP initiation and adherence. There were consistently low adherence and high discontinuation rates among AGYW with objective HIV risk behaviors. Prevention effectiveness and adherence varied with alignment and misalignment of behavioral risk and PrEP adherence. Decisions to use the vaginal ring instead of oral PrEP aligned with individual behavior. Dynamic changes in sexual behavior during PrEP use and decisions to switch to injectable PrEP where multiple alternatives are offered may be explored to support PrEP uptake and persistence.

items.title: Current Status of Tuberculosis and Human Immunodeficiency Virus Co-Infection in the Philippines: A Narrative Review.
items.authors: Teh TRD, Chua JJR, De Sagon SDP, Grecia MNI, Malaluan MV, Salvador PBU, Sanico TCF, Dalmacio LMM.
items.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection remains a major public health concern globally and in the Philippines. The country continues to face a high burden of TB, multidrug- and rifampicin-resistant TB (MDR/RR-TB), HIV, and HIV-associated TB. Since HIV increases the risk of TB and TB worsens HIV outcomes, co-infection hinders progress toward the End TB Strategy and the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets. This review summarizes the current knowledge on the epidemiology, prevention, and treatment of TB-HIV co-infection with a focus on the Philippine setting. Key challenges include socioeconomic barriers to care and rising drug resistance. In addition, the lack of an integrated TB-HIV data system disrupts continuity of care and weakens surveillance. Closing these gaps requires a coordinated national response that integrates effective policy with active community engagement. Research-driven and locally adapted strategies will be essential to bring the Philippines closer to its elimination goals.

items.title: A systematic review of evidence on weight change following initiation of long-acting cabotegravir for the prevention or treatment of HIV.
items.authors: Kitonsa J, Komata R, Ssembajjwe W, Grint D, Robinson J, Ruzagira E, Kalyesubula R, Vera J, Cresswell F.
items.abstract:
Background

Weight gain is an increasingly recognized concern among people receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) and may increase the risk of non-communicable diseases. Integrase inhibitors (INSTIs) such as dolutegravir (DTG) have been associated with weight gain, but the metabolic effects of long-acting cabotegravir (CAB-LA), another INSTI, for HIV treatment and prevention remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a systematic review to synthesize evidence on weight and body mass index (BMI) changes associated with CAB-LA-based regimens across ART and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) trials.

Methods

We systematically searched major biomedical databases, Medline, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, supplemented by Google Scholar and proceedings from key HIV conferences to identify grey literature for randomized controlled trials that evaluated CAB-LA as PrEP or CAB-LA-based regimen as ART between 01st January 2010 to 01st August 2025, with no language restrictions. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Given substantial heterogeneity in outcome reporting across studies, evidence was synthesized narratively following the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidance. Findings were summarized by intervention type (PrEP or ART), sex/gender and geographical setting.

Results

Of 1998 records identified, 234 were removed as duplicates, 1764 were screened at title and abstract level, and 42 full-text articles were assessed. This resulted in 11 reports from eight randomized controlled trials, with follow-up ranging from 41 to 185 weeks. Overall, weight remained stable or only increased modestly in both intervention and comparator groups across studies. Among HIV-negative individuals receiving CAB-LA for PrEP, weight gain was observed in both intervention and comparator groups, with no consistent evidence of excess weight gain attributable to CAB-LA. In HPTN 077, weight gain was similar between CAB-LA and placebo recipients, while HPTN 083 and HPTN 084 reported annualized weight gains ranging from 1.23 to 2.4 kg/year in CAB-LA recipients and 0.37 to 2.1 kg/year in comparator groups. Among people living with HIV receiving ART, weight changes at 48 weeks ranged from -0.4 to +1.8 kg with CAB-LA plus long-acting rilpivirine (RPV-LA) and 0.0 to +1.5 kg with comparator regimens, with no consistent evidence of greater weight gain in the CAB-LA plus RPV-LA arms. Only one trial among ART-experienced adults in Africa (CARES) reported greater weight gain with CAB-LA plus RPV-LA than with continued oral therapy (mean weight gain 1.5 kg vs. 0.0 kg, respectively), with more pronounced effects in women compared to men (2.1 kg vs. -0.2 kg). The overall risk of bias was low to moderate.

Conclusions

CAB-LA-based regimens were associated with only small increases in weight in both the prevention and treatment of HIV, with no consistent evidence of excess weight gain relative to standard comparators. Continued monitoring will be important as long-acting antiretroviral therapies are scaled up, particularly among women and individuals from Africa.

items.title: Delivering Long-Acting Injectable Cabotegravir PrEP to People Experiencing Homelessness and People Who Use Drugs.
items.authors: Mehtani NJ, Matzat SJ, Rustagi A, Stowe H, Strieff S, Sportsman D, Philbin MM, Gandhi M, Johnson MO.
items.abstract: Long-acting injectable cabotegravir (CAB-LA) may be particularly advantageous for preventing HIV among people experiencing homelessness (PEH) and people who use drugs (PWUD), populations at high HIV risk with poor oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) outcomes. In a retrospective study using the RE-AIM framework to organize programmatic outcomes, we evaluated real-world implementation of CAB-LA at the Maria X. Martinez Health Resource Center, a status-neutral, fully drop-in municipal clinic in San Francisco, CA, serving >4000 patients annually for diverse health needs. We included all patients prescribed CAB-LA between October 2022 and December 2025. Outcomes included reach, adoption, implementation (injection timeliness, delivery setting, guideline-concordant HIV monitoring), maintenance (retention), and exploratory effectiveness (HIV acquisitions relative to active coverage). Nineteen providers prescribed CAB-LA to 68 patients (63% experiencing homelessness; 56% with stimulant use disorder, 34% opioid use disorder, 51% psychotic-spectrum illness); 52 (76%) received ≥1 injection. Of 304 injections, 42% occurred outside the clinic, including in shelters, on the street, and in jail or inpatient settings; 76% of follow-up injections were on time. HIV testing concordant with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention guidelines (antigen/antibody plus RNA) accompanied 37% of injections. Twelve-month retention was 49%. Two patients acquired HIV, both during gaps in CAB-LA coverage. Sustaining coverage required intensive outreach, population tracking, insurance reenrollment, and financial incentives. Findings suggest that CAB-LA can be delivered in a fully drop-in clinic serving PEH and PWUD, while highlighting the resource-intensive support required to maintain coverage. Adapting delivery models, laboratory monitoring protocols, and financing to the realities of structurally vulnerable populations is essential to extend the benefits of long-acting PrEP.

items.title: Preferences for mobile HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis delivery among young men with alcohol use in rural South Africa: A discrete choice experiment.
items.authors: Castle AC, Mthembu NI, Nzimande L, Ncube T, Nkosi B, Dube S, Jarolimova J, Hoeppner SS, Shahmanesh M, Siedner MJ.
items.abstract:
Background

Young men who use alcohol have an elevated risk for HIV in South Africa but have low engagement with pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP).

Objectives

We conducted a discrete choice experiment (DCE) to explore preferences for mobile HIV prevention services in rural KwaZulu-Natal.

Method

Men aged ≥ 18 years with self-reported alcohol use participating in an HIV-prevention clinical trial completed a DCE. Attributes included clinic location (soccer fields, shebeens [informal bars], taxi ranks), operating hours (weekday, week-evening, weekend), and HIV prevention modality (event-driven oral PrEP, injectable PrEP, condoms only). Preferences were estimated using hierarchical Bayesian multinomial logit models. Relative attribute importance quantified each attribute's contribution to decision-making. Exploratory subgroup analyses examined variation by prior PrEP use, alcohol risk (AUDIT-C > 4), and age.

Results

Among 185 participants (mean age 27 years), HIV prevention modality was the most influential attribute (62.8% relative importance), followed by clinic location (26.3%) and clinic timing (10.9%). Services located at soccer fields were strongly preferred, while delivery at shebeens was disfavoured. Clinic timing showed minimal variation in preferences. Event-driven oral PrEP was preferred over condoms-only delivery, while injectable PrEP showed mixed preferences. Men with prior PrEP experience and high-risk alcohol use preferred injectable PrEP, whereas PrEP-naïve men and those with lower-risk drinking patterns preferred event-driven oral PrEP.

Conclusion

PrEP programmes for young men should pair prevention choice with acceptable service locations. Event-driven oral PrEP may be an entry point for PrEP-naïve men; injectable PrEP may appeal more to men with prior PrEP experience or higher-risk alcohol use.

items.title: The Views of Clients and Healthcare Professionals on the Perceived Effectiveness of HIV Prevention Programmes in Selected O. R. Tambo District Municipality Clinics.
items.authors: Mntonintshi TS, Boboyi A.
items.abstract:
Aim/background

This study examined the perceived effectiveness of HIV prevention programmes in the O.R. Tambo District Municipality from the perspectives of both clients and healthcare professionals. Although a range of interventions is available-such as condom distribution, HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), and prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT)-HIV prevalence in the area remains high.

Methods

A qualitative, exploratory design guided by the Health Belief Model (HBM) was employed to explore the factors influencing the utilisation of these services. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with clients and focus group discussions with healthcare professionals. Participants were selected using purposive sampling, and the data were analysed thematically.

Results

The findings show that the perceived effectiveness of these programmes is shaped by several factors, including adherence, service accessibility, stigma, and levels of knowledge and awareness. While participants generally acknowledged the benefits of the programmes, their impact was limited by inconsistent use, restricted access, and prevailing misconceptions.

Conclusions

The study concludes that there is a need to strengthen educational efforts, improve access to services, and address social barriers in order to enhance programme utilisation and ultimately reduce HIV transmission.
